answer.thought: The bookseller watches me with the polite indifference of a man who has seen many Europeans and few philosophers. My stomach, however, makes no such distinctions; it is a concrete particular that demands satisfaction now. I have only ninety-six rupees, and the chole bhature costs one hundred and eighty. I cannot spend what I do not have, but the hunger is a universal that overrides my particular financial constraint. I will wait, and perhaps the system of needs will provide a way, or I shall simply have to endure the contradiction of a full mind and an empty body.
